newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes rise moderately late Wed..
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes rise moderately late Wed..

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes rose moderately in late Wednesday trade, tracking a spot crude market concerned about low heating oil inventories.
West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 35 cents as bullish fundamentals for heating oil reversed early weakness sparked by reports of milder temperatures in the U.S. northeast.
Alaska North Slope crude (ANS) followed WTI's 35 cent rise, ranging $24.25/24.45 a barrel amid flat differentials.
ANS crude for spot sales remained at a $1.70 discount to WTI, after nearly five days without sales.
"I can't see people racing to buy ANS at $1.60 under $26," a barrel, a buyer said. She referred to January crude futures breaking a Post-Gulf War high of $26.10 late Wednesday.
A major ANS producer set the $1.60 price, while a large refiner led bids with a minus $2.25 price, traders said.
Line 63 crude was thin, with no fixed basis deals and posted plus values stagnant at $0.95 to $1.05.
Kern River prices stayed $18.15/18.25 a barrel late after rising Monday on increased posted prices.
Discounts remained 10 cents below to even with postings, traders said.
Wilmington crude, produced offshore in Long Beach, Calif., also rose with postings Monday to $19.65/19.75.
